**Considered and rejected:** - `guard.brand.<artwork>` - 60 suites; the rule turns into a formality filled in by copy-paste; - one common `guard.brand` for everything - it loses what a guard exists for: the installer suite and the file-type-icon suite check different contracts (an opaque background against transparency, one frame against nine); - deriving the guard from the container instead of the family - `icon` lives in five containers at once and their drawing is one; splitting it by container means splitting one contract.
**When to revisit:** if one family ends up holding artworks with different contracts - then the family has stopped being a guard group and has to split.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-ARTWORK-SUBDIR:
**Decision:** the artworks of a family with several drawings live in a subdirectory of the family - `branding/filetype/json.svg`; the flat form `branding/icon.svg` is kept for a family with one drawing.
**Why:** The flat name `filetype-json.svg` would collide in meaning with the already occupied form `<key>-<N>.png`: one and the same hyphen would mean a size in one place and the name of a drawing in another, and the reader of a directory of sixty files could not tell an override from an artwork except by checking whether the tail consists of digits. A subdirectory separates the two meanings syntactically rather than by convention, and it makes the masters directory readable into the bargain: one family, one folder.
**Considered and rejected:** - flat names with a hyphen - the collision of meanings described above; - a separate index file mapping a target to a master - one more document that has to be kept from going stale; the whole command is built on the opposite principle (`##DECISION-IMAGESET-INDEX-IS-COMPUTED`); - a directory for EVERY family, the single ones included - `branding/icon/icon.svg` stutters, and there is no reason to demand a migration of the existing flat masters.
**When to revisit:** if a family with one drawing gains a second one - then its master moves into a subdirectory, and that is the only migration the convention allows.

p.DECISION-IMAGESET-VECTOR-PASSTHROUGH:
**Decision:** an SVG target is delivered byte for byte from the vector master; no rendering, no normalization, no rewriting of the document.
**Why:** The application loads these files as vectors and scales them itself. Rasterizing a vector in order to hand a raster to a place that expects a vector is a loss without a gain; normalizing the document (rewriting the paths, cleaning out the attributes) means taking on the responsibility that the drawing did not change after the rewrite, and that can be checked only by rasterization, which is the very thing we wanted to avoid. An empty diff on a repeated regeneration comes free here, because the bytes were never touched.
**Considered and rejected:** - rasterizing to PNG and swapping the reference - it changes how the application loads the resource, that is, it patches upstream code for the sake of a picture; - running it through an SVG optimizer - a new dependency, output that is not deterministic across versions, and the same uncheckability of the result; - not checking the size of the master - a watermark of the wrong size would travel into the product silently, and it would be seen in the layout.
**When to revisit:** if upstream starts assembling these SVGs from a template at build time - then the target stops being a file, and the delivery has to move into a layer that can patch the generator.

p.LICENSE-NAMESPACE: `license` is a namespace (like `imageset`): a bare `codkit license` and an unknown subcommand print the list of subcommands and exit 2 through `usageFail`, before the roots are resolved; it has no `--help` of its own - the command reference answers the question about it. The subcommands: `check`, `annotate`, `notices`.

p.CMD-LICENSE-CHECK: `codkit license check [<dir>]` is the check of the licence markup of a package directory per PROP-014 §3 (`LIC-CHECK-ALGORITHM`): the carriers of every file in REUSE precedence order, the own/third-party classification, the `REUSE.toml` registry and the allowlist, orphan sidecars, and the consistency of `vibe.toml`/`LICENSE`/`LICENSES/`/`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. `<dir>` is a path (relative to cwd or absolute); without the argument it is the standards package from toolRoot (PROP-014 `STD-PACKAGE-LOCATION`). No roots are needed (`roots: 'none'`, `configMode: 'none'`): checking a directory does not have to know a patch set. Read-only; git is not called; symbolic links are not resolved. The output is `LIC-CHECK-REPORT`; `--json` is `data: {dir, files, checked, problems, policy}`. Codes: 0 clean; 1 there are problems (`CK-E-LICENSE-HEADER`, `CK-E-LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY`, `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE`); 2 the environment (no directory, a broken policy or SPDX list - `CK-E-CONFIG`, an unreadable file). It is idempotent.

p.CMD-LICENSE-ANNOTATE: `codkit license annotate [--dir <package>] <paths…> [--dry-run] [--year <YYYY>] [--holder <name>] [--third-party --license <SPDX-ID> --source <text>]` places the carrier (PROP-014 §3 `LIC-ANNOTATE`): on an own file a four-line header in the style of its extension, after the prelude, or a sidecar; on a third-party file (`--third-party`, and then `--holder` and `--license` are required) a carrier with the other party's holder and licence plus an annotation appended to the end of `REUSE.toml`. It is idempotent: a file that already carries its markup is `unchanged`. No roots are needed (`roots: 'none'`, `configMode: 'none'`); `maxArgs` is not limited (the paths); the flags `--dir`, `--year`, `--holder`, `--license`, `--source` take values, `--third-party` is boolean, and `--dry-run` is the common one. `--json`: `data: {dir, files: [{path, action: "header"|"sidecar"|"unchanged", kind}], registry: {path, appended}}`. Codes: 0; 1 (a path outside `--dir`, a licence outside the allowlist or not an SPDX one, a holder outside the policy without `--third-party`, `--third-party` without `--holder`/`--license`); 2 (the environment).

p.CMD-LICENSE-NOTICES: `codkit license notices [--dir <package>] [--dry-run]` generates `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` from the registry (PROP-014 §2 `LIC-NOTICES-FILE`, §3 `LIC-NOTICES`): a non-empty registry → the file is written atomically (`written`/`unchanged`); an empty one → there is no file, and an existing one is removed with a printed line (`removed`); `--dry-run` prints the result to stdout without writing. No roots are needed. `--json`: `data: {dir, path, action, rows}`. Codes: 0; 1 (`REUSE.toml` does not parse, or an annotation is incomplete); 2 (the environment).

p.STANDARDS-NAMESPACE: `standards` is a namespace: a bare `codkit standards` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2 before the roots are resolved; the subcommands are `load`, `check` and `license`. The first two need patchesDir and `codkit.json` (`configMode: 'load'`; the fork tree is not read, the tree lock is not taken), because the packages delivered are the universal ones plus the ones the patch set's project type names (PROP-014 `STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`), and `license` needs no root at all (`roots: 'none'`); under `--ci` all three are allowed - there is no network. In an agent session over the product repository all three are outside the read-only allowlist of the hook (`load` writes; `check`/`license` are candidates for the allowlist and are deferred) - these are commands of a human or of an orchestrator.

p.CMD-STANDARDS-LOAD: `codkit standards load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` delivers **every shipped package** (`standards`, `agent-skills`; PROP-014 `STD-SHIPPED-PACKAGES`, `STD-LOAD-ALL-PACKAGES`) into the product repository (the algorithm is PROP-014 §5); at the end come the lines `next: vibe install --offline` (after `--upgrade`, `vibe install --offline --force`) and, when a package carries skills, `next: vibe skill install`. `--upgrade` replaces a drifted or outdated copy as a whole (PROP-014 `STD-LOAD-UPGRADE`, `DECISION-STD-MUTABLE-EDITION`). Order: the package in toolRoot → the licence check of the package (a failure is a report, exit 1 and not a single write; there is no bypass flag) → the preconditions of the manifest (`vibe.toml` with `[project]`, without CR) and the classification of the block → the classification of the target `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/standards/v<version>/` (`absent` / `identical` / `drift`) → `--dry-run` prints the plan and exits with the same code without writing → the files are written into a temporary directory and renamed → the two copies of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` (the product root and `delta/own/`, PROP-014 §4a) → the manifest block → the block of rows in `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` when the contract exists (PROP-014 §4a `STD-SCRAPE-STATE-MACHINE`; its absence is the information `no-contract`) → the summary with `next: vibe install --offline`, the note about the licences (`STD-LOAD-LICENCE-NOTE`) and the recommendations for the notice file (`STD-LOAD-NOTICE-PRINT`). Side effects: the version directory in the product's `vibevm/vibepacks/` (a byte-for-byte copy), the two copies of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, the block in `vibe.toml`, the block in an existing `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml`; nothing more - `vibe` is not called, and `vibe.lock` and `vibedeps` are not touched. A repeat is `up to date`, exit 0, with not a byte changed. Codes: 0; 1 (`CK-E-LICENSE-*` of the package; `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` - the installed copy of the package or the copy of `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` differs, with the list of `modified`/`extra`/`missing`; `CK-E-CONFIG` - the manifest block or the scrape-contract block is malformed, a package entry or a notice row is outside its own block; `CK-E-CRLF`); 2 (no `vibe.toml`, or no `[project]` in it - `CK-E-CONFIG` with a hint about `vibe init`; no permissions; a corrupted installation - `CK-E-INTERNAL`). `--json`: `data` per PROP-014 `STD-LOAD-STEP-REPORT`.

p.CMD-STANDARDS-CHECK: `codkit standards check` is read-only (PROP-014 §6): the state of the installed copy (`absent`/`identical`/`drift` with the list), the licence check of the copy, the state of both `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` copies, the state of the manifest block (`absent`/`current`/`stale`/`malformed`/`entry-outside-block`), the state of the scrape-contract block (`no-contract` is information, not a finding; otherwise the same five states), a warning about a tail after the block, and other versions alongside. Codes: 0 - `identical` plus a clean copy plus `current`; 1 - any finding, each on a line of its own with a code (`CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT`, `CK-E-LICENSE-*`, `CK-E-CONFIG`) and the hint `run codkit standards load`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {target, license, noticeFiles, manifest, scrape, otherVersions}`.

p.CMD-STANDARDS-LICENSE: `codkit standards license` only prints and needs no root (`roots: 'none'`, `configMode: 'none'`, `maxArgs: 0`, no flags): the full text of the file `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` that `load` places in the two roots of the product; then the recommendations - where the copies live, that nobody edits them, that links to the file are placed by the product owner alone, from the README of the product and from the patch-set intervention in the README of the fork, and where the three licence scopes end; then, verbatim, the two rows of the `vibe scrape` contract (`[[classify]]` delete and `[[assert]]` paths-absent for `LICENSE-CODKIT.md` and `delta/own/LICENSE-CODKIT.md`) - the very rows `standards load` maintains in the product's `vibevm/scrape/contract.toml` itself; they are printed for a contract at a non-standard path (`vibe scrape --contract`) and for review (PROP-014 §4a `STD-SCRAPE-CONTRACT-ROWS`); then the ready `[[annotations]]` entry for the product's `REUSE.toml` (`STD-LICENSE-PRINTS-REUSE-ROWS`). The text of the file is printed with a components block computed for patchesDir when one is given (`--patches-dir` or the configuration), and otherwise with an empty block and a note. `--json`: `data: {file: "LICENSE-CODKIT.md", text, recommendations: [...], scrapeContractRows, reuseAnnotation}`. Codes: 0; 2 - the environment only (an unreadable shipped file - `CK-E-INTERNAL`).

p.RUNTIME-NAMESPACE: `runtime` is a namespace modeled on `standards`: a bare `codkit runtime` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2 before the roots are resolved; the subcommands are `load` and `check`; both need only patchesDir (`configMode: 'none'`, the tree is not read, the tree lock is not taken); under `--ci` they are allowed - there is no network. In an agent session over the product repository, `load` is outside the read-only allowlist of the hook.

p.CMD-RUNTIME-LOAD: `codkit runtime load [--dry-run] [--upgrade]` delivers the runtime library into the product's `delta/own/codkit/` (the algorithm is PROP-015 §4 `RT-LOAD-STEPS`): the source in toolRoot → the licence check of the version directory (a failure is exit 2 and not a single write) → the classification of the target (`absent` / `identical` / `drift`; a `drift` without `--upgrade` is exit 1) → `--dry-run` prints the plan → the write through a temporary directory → the notice copies with the components block (PROP-014 §4a) → the summary with three hints (the graft in the composition root, the `code-import-patterns` block from `LAYERS.md`, `codkit gen feature`). A warning when the product's `pin.tag` is not in `CODKIT_RUNTIME_VERIFIED_UPSTREAM`. `--json`: `data: {version, target, state, files:{written, removed}, notice, verifiedUpstream:boolean}`. Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT`; 2 - `CK-E-RUNTIME-PACKAGE`, `CK-E-LICENSE-PACKAGE`, the environment.

p.CMD-RUNTIME-CHECK: `codkit runtime check` is read-only (PROP-015 `RT-CHECK`): the state of the installed copy (`absent` is the information `runtime not installed`, `identical`, `drift` with the list), the state of both notice copies and `legacy-copy`. Codes: 0 - `identical`, or `absent` while the notice copies are clean; 1 - `CK-E-RUNTIME-DRIFT` / `CK-E-STANDARDS-DRIFT` (the notice copies) with the hint `run codkit runtime load --upgrade`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {target:{state, version, paths}, noticeFiles}`.

p.GEN-NAMESPACE: `gen` is a namespace: a bare `codkit gen` and an unknown subcommand give the list of subcommands and exit 2; the subcommands are `feature` and `brand`; both read the patch set's configuration (`configMode: 'load'`), because the skeleton and the graft are the project type's answer and the type is named there (PROP-016 `TYPE-AREA-GENERATORS`); no fork tree is needed. Flags: `--title <text>` (a value), `--setting`, `--cold` (boolean), `--holder`, `--license`, `--year` (values, as for `license annotate`), `--header-style line|block`, `--header-file <path>` (values; PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`).

p.CMD-GEN-FEATURE: `codkit gen feature <id> --title <text> [--setting] [--cold] [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` is the skeleton of a product feature (PROP-015 §5 `GEN-FEATURE`, `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`, `GEN-TEST-LIVES-WITH-THE-FEATURE`, `GEN-REFUSES-EXISTING`): three files under `delta/own/contrib/<name>/` (the test in the `test/browser/` of the feature), the import line for the composition root and the reminder about the unit. Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; 2 - `CK-E-GEN-ID`, a missing `--title`, incompatible header flags, an unreadable `--header-file`, the environment. `--json`: `data: {id, files:[…], importLine, headerWritten:boolean, headerStyle: "line"|"block"|"file"|null}`.

p.CMD-GEN-BRAND: `codkit gen brand [--holder …] [--license …] [--year …] [--header-style line|block] [--header-file <path>]` is the scaffold of the brand table (the header flags are the same as for `gen feature`, PROP-015 `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS`) `delta/own/common/brand.ts`, plus the printing of the hook text for `_format` with its reminders (PROP-015 `GEN-BRAND`). Codes: 0; 1 - `CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`; 2 - the environment. `--json`: `data: {file, hookText, reminders:[…]}`.

p.CMD-PACKAGE: Build the product's distributable out of the already loaded fork tree. It exists because `ci --profile build` stops at the compile channels and the own tests: until this verb, `build.packageBuild` was a field of the type contract that no module of the engine read, and the last step of a release was a sequence of commands typed by hand whose two ends people got wrong. The order of one run is fixed and is printed before it starts: (1) the drift guard of `load` - unextracted work is `CK-E-DIRTY-TREE`, exit 1, and the one exemption is the one `load --fresh` makes, a tracked overlay target carrying exactly the strict composition of the configured overlays (PROP-005 §5 `##OVERLAY-KNOWN-MATERIALIZATION`), which a previous `--keep-overlay` run may have left; (2) the overlay targets are materialized into the tree, because a packaged product reads the target file itself and not the dev-channel sidecar; (3) the stamps the type names (`build.packageStamps`) are put into the environment of the commands below, filled from the tree head, the pin or the type's own answer - except a name the operator already exported with a non-empty value, which keeps the operator's value and is printed as `stamp <name>=<value> (from environment)` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-STAMPS-FILL-A-GAP`); (4) `build.packageBuild` of the type runs in the tree, each command's whole output printed; (5) then `build.packageDistributable` - the packaging step the patch set declared - runs on the same terms; (6) the existing artifacts matching `build.packageOutputs` are printed; (6a) the paths the type names as the residue of its packaging (`build.packageScratch`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`) are returned to the tip of the loaded tree - only the tracked ones that changed, whatever the verdict of the packaging, and **also under `--keep-overlay`**, which keeps the materialization and never the residue; (7) the overlay targets **this run materialized itself** are returned to the pin and the dev channel is rewritten, exactly as `load --fresh --discard` does for those files - not a fresh pass: build outputs, dependency roots and everything else in the tree are left alone. Step 7 runs whatever the verdict of steps 4-5, so a build that fails halfway never leaves a developer's tree in packaging state. It is not a daemon, so the wrapper of §13 does not apply and `--timeout <seconds>` bounds one command instead of one pass; it holds the per-tree lock like every writing command. Flags: `--keep-overlay` (skip step 7 - never step 6a - for a hand check of the package in the tree; `codkit load --fresh` is the way back), `--skip-type-build` (skip step 4, when the watch channels already built the application), `--timeout <seconds>`, `--json`. There is deliberately **no `--discard`**: giving up somebody's unextracted work is never a side effect of packaging, and the guard of this command may only be narrowed by codkit's own materialization. Codes: 0; 1 - the guard, or a packaging command that exited non-zero (`CK-E-PACKAGE-FAILED`, naming the label, the exit code and the tail of what the command printed); 2 - the environment (an unusable tree, a command that could not be started at all, a malformed `--timeout`). `--json`: `data: {steps:[{name,state,detail}], materialized:[…], restored:[…], scratchRestored:[…], stamps:{…}, stampsFromEnvironment:[…], commands:[…], outputs:[…]}`.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-TARGETS: `codkit package [<selector>]` accepts an exact type-owned target id, a platform family (`windows`, `linux`, `macos`) or `all`. With no selector it uses `typeConfig` through the configured type's `defaultPackageTargets`. A family selector and `all` retain only recipes whose `supportedHosts` includes the current OS; an exact incompatible target refuses rather than attempting an unproved cross-build. The selected ids are printed before the plan and returned as `data.targets`.

p.CMD-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS-STAY-IN-THE-TREE: Where the artifact lands is the type's answer and the answer is **tree-relative** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`). A family whose packager writes into a sibling directory of the managed tree therefore names no output at all, and the command says so - `the project type <id> names no package output inside the tree` - instead of printing a path the tool neither manages, guards, nor cleans. This is a refusal to widen the tool's reach, not a gap: the operator reads the location from the packager's own output, which the command printed in full.

p.COMMAND-ROSTER: `where`, `check-tree`, `clone`, `load`, `status`, `save`, `sync`, `gc`, `marker new`, `reresolve`, `inventory`, `verify`, `overlay new|apply|check`, `build up|down|status|errors`, `cycle start|continue|status|restart`, `forecast`, `rebase-onto-pin`, `ci`, `publish`, `hooks install|check`, `imageset`, `license check|annotate|notices`, `standards load|check|license`, `runtime load|check`, `gen feature|brand`, `package`. Planned (PROP-016): `types`.

p.CMD-TYPES-XREF: `codkit types` - the contract of the verb lives in `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#CMD-TYPES` and is not restated here: it prints the registered types, their package and version and the capability matrix, needs no patch set and writes nothing. Two more facts of PROP-016 bind the roster to the types: every verb keeps its name, flags and exit codes and names the type where it matters (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-VERBS-UNIVERSAL`), and a verb whose capability the type does not declare refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` before any write (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`).
